noi_dung:
The Secret of Chan Investigation

The word "Chan" translates as "still consideration," also as "cultivation through reflection." Reflection is precisely investigating; still consideration means "time and again, wipe it diligently; let no dust alight." Practicing cultivation through reflection means we must raise up the hua-tou, ever mindful, never apart for an instant. There is a saying: "Morning thus, evening thus." Apply effort through the own-nature; seek nothing outside. Meeting states then chasing states, you go astray. States born from the own-nature are true states. May you truly grasp this point—or you will fall to the Demon King, becoming his kin.

The still-consideration Dharma-door demands unbroken, close-woven effort, never pausing. Such effort may be likened to the mother hen wholeheartedly hatching her eggs, the dragon carefully nurturing its pearl, and the cat patiently stalking the mouse. Chan investigation requires a resolute mind, a sincere mind, and a constant mind. Never an arrogant mind, deeming yourself higher or finer than others. With such thoughts, madness demons enter, rendering skill fruitless.

In Chan investigation, give rise to no discursive thoughts. With discursive thoughts, no benefit at all—only wasted time and skill. Chan investigation requires a patient mind, a long-range mind—thinking long-term. The secret of Chan investigation is the word patience; what cannot be borne must still be borne; bearing to the extreme, suddenly penetrating, brightly enlightened. Without patience, unwilling to bear suffering and toil, meeting obstacles you will surely surrender. Such ways are unacceptable—most taboo in Chan investigation.
